newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-KOSTNER DRESSED FOR SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-KOSTNER DRESSED FOR SUCCESS.

text.p: Isolde Kostner said on Tuesday she'd put her lucky undershirt on the auction block -- when she's finished with it.
But that could be a long time coming.

The superstitious Italian was wearing her lucky T-shirt when she successfully defended her super-giant slalom title at the Alpine skiing world championships and will pull it out of the drawer again on Saturday as she goes in search of a second gold in the downhill.

Deborah Compagnoni, already a double gold medallist with victories in the giant slalom and slalom, donated a picture she painted while relaxing at the championships to a charity auction and raised 18 million lira.
Kostner, 21, refused to speculate what her tattered undershirt might pull in, but with many more races ahead of her, there might not be much left when she's finally through with it.

"I don't know when I'll change it," said Kostner, who first wore the shirt in 1994. "I've worn it when I haven't won races but I was also wearing it when I won (an Olympic bronze medal) in Lillehammer.
"It's a trivial thing but you never know."
Kostner is also superstitious about numbers -- particularly two of the same.
After selecting the eighth start number on Monday Kostner woke in a cold sweat on Tuesday morning when she realised she had set her alarm for eight o'clock.
She reset her alarm for eight minutes after eight and went back to sleep, later explaining that, "three numbers the same is good".
Kostner may not change her racing undergarments but she is changing some habits.
She said she would not celebrate Tuesday's win in the same manner as last year's victory in Sierra Nevada, Spain when she sang and danced into the early hours.
Instead she planned a quiet dinner with sponsors and a few friends.
"I want to concentrate on the downhill," said Kostner. "But it wasn't the celebrations that kept me from winning the downhill in Spain.
"The next day I was the fastest in training and I was fastest all week -- the only time I wasn't was in the race."
